issues.what: Akkadian -2300 keyframe snap (904 cells added, 390 removed): the keyframe is Cliopatria's -2300 shape minus Khuzestan; the 390 removed cells are desert fringe (Al-Muthannia, An-Najaf, Al-Basrah) of the ledger's broad 'Sumer' region, left unowned, and Sumer proper (Dhi-Qar, Maysan, Qadisiyyah) goes to Akkad on Sargon's conquest.

Akkadian -2250 keyframe snap (242 cells added, 6 removed): Naram-Sin's peak shape reaching northern Syria and the Cilician coast; matches Cliopatria and the dossier's reading of Naram-Sin's campaigns.
Sumerian city-states -2300 snap (32 cells): small ledger gap at the end of the state's life, absorbed by Akkad the same year.

Indus Valley Civilization jumps from 227 to 3027 cells in -2300 (ledger/4, 2800 cells). It is explained by an event dated to Cliopatria's full-extent shape; the dossier's own note puts the Mature Harappan phase at c. 2600-1900 BCE, so an earlier spread is arguable, but any change belongs to the -2500 keyframe in the earlier windows, outside this window.

Akkadian Empire holds 50 cells of the United Arab Emirates (Magan) from -2250 to the end anchor, while the dossier's -2250, -2240 and -2220 corrections remove only the country Oman as 'campaigns, not held land'. Magan page: 'an ancient region in what is now modern day Oman and United Arab Emirates'; 'Akkadian campaigns against Magan took place in the twenty-third century BCE'; Naram-Sin and Manishtusu wrote of campaigning against '32 lords of Magan' and Naram-Sin 'not only conquered Magan'. The page supports a conquest claim, so the treatment of Oman and the UAE is inconsistent but neither is clearly wrong; left for the dossier owner. The -2200 keyframe (next window) re-adds Oman at 1 Jan -2200 (Cliopatria's shape, no Oman removal).
issues.decision: left: page supports conquest of Magan, no clear error
